goal: Explain why the renamed self-contained single-file WinUI executable can no longer find its MRT resources and give a project-file workaround or upgrade path.
must_include: Connects the XamlParseException to renaming the published single-file executable, not to a broken MainWindow XAML element.
Says the resource lookup is derived from the executable name in affected SDK builds, so the renamed exe looks for the wrong PRI/resource name.
Adds `<ProjectPriFileName>resources.pri</ProjectPriFileName>` in a project property group or tells the developer to update to the Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.MSIX build that contains the fix.
Keeps `WindowsAppSDKSelfContained`/single-file deployment as a supported publishing choice but notes the native Windows App SDK files and PRI resources still must be present.
must_not: Tell the developer to catch and ignore XamlParseException in `OnLaunched`.
Advise renaming or deleting `.pri` files by hand after publish.
Claim WinUI 3 supports a completely standalone one-file executable with no resource files.
acceptable_alternatives: Do not rename the published executable and instead set the assembly/output name before publishing.
Move to a fixed Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.MSIX package instead of carrying the explicit `ProjectPriFileName` workaround.
solved: The answer identifies the rename-dependent PRI lookup failure and gives either the `ProjectPriFileName` workaround or the fixed SDK package/update path.
partial: The answer recognizes a missing resource/PRI problem but does not tie it to the renamed executable or gives no durable workaround.
notes: The issue was reported against Windows App SDK 1.8-era bits and later comments cite a BuildTools.MSIX fix; the workaround is still useful when the project is pinned to affected packages.
